extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners working on federated learning, privacy-preserving machine learning, and related systems/cryptography/statistics
extracted.subtask_description: A broad literature survey and discussion of open problems in federated learning that summarizes recent advances, system challenges, privacy/threat models, and research directions. Intended to scope further research across multiple disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency under system constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The system constraints impose efficiency requirements on the algorithms in order to be practical, many of which are not particularly challenging in other settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithms for federated learning must be designed for limited client resources (computation, memory, communication, intermittent connectivity, energy) and for communication-efficiency and scalability; methods that work in centralized settings may be impractical. Evaluation should measure communication/computation trade-offs and client-resource usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat privacy as a spectrum / explicit threat models
rubrics_metrics.description: We argue that data privacy is not binary and present a range of threat models that are relevant under a variety of assumptions, each of which provides its own unique challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should explicitly state and justify the privacy threat model (e.g., honest-but-curious server, malicious clients, external adversaries, reconstruction attacks) and analyze protections relative to that model. Claims of 'privacy' should be qualified by the assumed adversary capabilities and evaluated under appropriate attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of non-learning decentralized tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not discuss any non-learning problems which need to be solved in the course of a practical machine learning project, and might need to be solved based on decentralized data. This can include simple problems such as computing basic descriptive statistics, or more complex objectives such as computing the head of a histogram over an open set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federated solutions should either provide or integrate primitives for non-learning tasks (statistics, aggregates, preprocessing) with attention to efficiency and data-protection. Evaluations should include whether such auxiliary tasks admit efficient federated versions and maintain the desired privacy guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of interdisciplinary trade-offs and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Federated learning is gaining traction in a wide range of interdisciplinary fields: from machine learning to optimization to information theory and statistics to cryptography, fairness, and privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should locate contributions relative to multiple relevant disciplines, acknowledging trade-offs (e.g., optimization vs. privacy vs. cryptographic overhead vs. fairness). Comparative evaluation should draw on metrics and baselines from the relevant subfields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize open-problem scope and author perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: The open problems discussed in this work are certainly not comprehensive, they reflect the interests and backgrounds of the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting open problems or research agendas, be explicit about scope and selection bias; clarify which areas are intentionally out-of-scope. Readers and evaluators should treat the listed open problems as illustrative, not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical deployment constraints including legal and business issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Yet another set of important topics that were not discussed are the legal and business issues that may motivate or constrain the use of federated learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work intended for real-world deployment should consider regulatory, legal, and business constraints (data protection laws, contractual constraints, product incentives) that impact feasibility and design choices. Empirical or systems papers should discuss these constraints or justify their omission.
